title: Goldhill Reprocessing: End-to-End Validation of Corrected Drone Imagery
intro: The new source is a more faithful numerical preprocessing input. It does not yet support an approved physical correction or official spectral library.
findings: The report separates actual production calls, unsupported stages and unchanged historical replays. No scientific safeguard was disabled.
The red stripe persists in the historical BRDF replay. A visually improved source does not repair an unsupported correction model.

title: A better numerical source, with the physical question still open
intro: The original approximately 8.44 cm UInt16 orthomosaic was converted directly to 10 cm using S = DN x 10000 / 65535. There is no band-minimum subtraction, clipping or integer quantization.

figure.name: figure01_sources
figure.caption: Actual raw sources, RGB=650/560/475 nm. A common new-raw 2-98% RGB stretch is applied to all three after the explicit original-to-fixed numerical encoding. White is missing/transparent; no corrected image or physical calibration is implied.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: The declared original alpha mask excludes transparent samples before bilinear interpolation. The new file has ten spectral bands and an internal GDAL validity mask.
Nominal encoding 0-10,000 does not force each observed band to fill that interval. Physical reflectance calibration remains UNVERIFIED.

title: Background is no longer treated as observed signal
intro: All 537,552 occurrences of 65,535 in each original band lie in transparent background. None is a measured saturated pixel. The historical interpolation allowed this background to mix into boundary pixels.

figure.name: figure02_background
figure.caption: All maps use the same grid/extent. Left codes: 0 missing both, 1 old-only, 2 new-only, 3 both. Middle uses the recovered fixed encoding, separating minimum normalization from interpolation/masks. The >2 display flag is a diagnostic threshold, not a scientific approval rule.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: New source support: 6,683,944 pixels. Historical finite-H5 support: 7,068,376 pixels. These counts are not equivalent observation masks.

Within the new footprint, 3,244 old red-band values exceed the original observed maximum under the same fixed encoding. The new source excludes transparent samples during interpolation; no value clipping is used.

title: Aligned inputs do not establish correct solar provenance
intro: Actual TIFF-to-H5 and H5-to-ENVI package functions preserved all finite values and missingness, EPSG:26913, the affine grid, band order and source footprint. Sensor viewing datasets were deliberately not created.

figure.name: figure03_ancillary
figure.caption: Terrain/solar grids align with the new TIFF. Original photo tags now support the inherited August 15 scene timestamp despite the nominal August 14 package note/name. Explicit time-zone/clock validation and per-pixel camera assignments remain unresolved.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: Wavelengths: 444, 475, 531, 560, 650, 668, 705, 717, 740, 862 nm. FWHM: 28, 32, 14, 27, 16, 14, 10, 12, 18, 57 nm, inherited from the established source H5.

Inherited solar metadata says 2023-08-15T19:53:07; original package notes identify 2023-08-14 at 13:41 local. The original photo metadata supports August 15: all 5,650 linked cameras match unique August 15 tags; the inherited solar time is 5.5 seconds from their midpoint. Explicit time-zone/clock and per-pixel time assignments remain unverified.

title: Camera orientations arrived; the per-pixel observation model did not
intro: The supplied CSV contains camera locations and band-specific rotations, which improves the available provenance. It does not identify the camera observations or blend weights contributing to each mosaic pixel.

figure.name: figure05_camera_support
figure.caption: Points are shown in the reported coordinate numbers without silently relabeling the CRS or assigning footprints. Current source H5 deliberately has no sensor-view datasets. Historical zero-view controls are not treated as measured observations.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: The CSV states CRS 5070, while its coordinate values fall with the TIFF in UTM 13N / EPSG:26913. The CRS and angular/vertical conventions need confirmation.

Actual production BRDF receives no per-pixel sensor angles. The direct fit reports missing sensor_zn; the correction driver reports UNSUPPORTED. The known legacy zero-view control has rank 1 of 3, but is not treated as measured viewing geometry.

title: Photo metadata supports August 15 and the inherited scene midpoint
intro: The nominal August 14 package name/note conflicts with the original photo tags. All 6,095 raw metadata rows are dated August 15; all 5,650 supplied camera records join uniquely, without missing or ambiguous IDs.

figure.name: figure13_photo_times
figure.caption: Matched camera records span 19:42:38-20:03:47 on August 15. The midpoint is 19:53:12.5, only 5.5 seconds from the inherited solar timestamp. Numerical agreement supports that timestamp; explicit clock/time-zone accuracy and mosaic pixel contributors are not established.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: Matched timestamps span 19:42:38-20:03:47. Their midpoint is 19:53:12.5; the inherited solar computation used 19:53:07. This is positive source evidence for that scene timestamp, not a reason to discard it based only on the package name.

The CSV does not state the time zone or independently verify camera clock accuracy. Per-photo times are now recoverable by ID, but each orthomosaic pixel still needs its contributing images/weights before those times and views can be assigned scientifically.

title: Production functions executed; refused stages stay refused
intro: Each result below comes from an actual package call. A raw export or native-band subset is an uncalibrated numerical product, not a physical correction.
findings: The caller initially omitted output directories for the raw-copy and matched-subset helpers. Those setup errors were corrected and the actual calls rerun successfully; initial outcomes and both logs are retained.

No alternate correction algorithm, neutral current coefficient set or fabricated calibration was substituted. The normal drone route uses native MicaSense band selection and versioned bulk-affine Landsat plans; no hyperspectral SRF convolution was fabricated from ten sparse bands.

title: Historical SCS+C is a stress test, not approval
intro: The unchanged historical fit/application functions were replayed with the new encoded source and inherited terrain/solar arrays. Their model guards are retained and all output magnitudes remain uncapped.

figure.name: figure04_scs_factors
figure.caption: Only the unchanged historical implementation is replayed here; current production SCS+C is blocked by calibration. Color under/over triangles expose values beyond 0.1-10; analytical maxima are retained. The red maximum is 309.9 near a 0.001 denominator.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: Red factor maximum: 309.9 at row 1178, column 1533. Slope is 41.89 degrees, illumination cosine 0.34826, fitted C=-0.34725, denominator 0.001005. This is near cancellation of model terms, not proof of a valid 310-fold physical illumination adjustment.

On common support, 11,305 red pixels receive factors above 10. Current production SCS+C was blocked. Missing calibration, unverified time-zone/per-pixel timing and this numerical instability prevent a defensible production recommendation.

section: 4. What happened to the red stripe?
title: Source repair does not repair the historical BRDF denominator
intro: The unchanged saved model and historical code were applied only inside the explicitly marked replay namespace. The source change leaves the old geometry/model mechanism in place.

figure.name: figure06_red_stripe
figure.caption: Same previously selected 50.1 x 40.1 m ROI, same RGB=650/560/475 nm and display limits. Historical corrections are unsupported diagnostics. Extremely large red values saturate this display; uncapped values and jumps are reported numerically.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: The new raw image has no comparable algorithmic red discontinuity. The historical replay still turns ordinary red-band values into billions of encoded units.

Saved neutral coefficients in historically under-supported bands remain historical evidence, not successful new fits. Current package safeguards do not silently replace the missing fit with neutral coefficients.

section: 4. What happened to the red stripe?
title: Measure the discontinuity on a fixed boundary
intro: A previously defined row/ROI and 2,934 boundary edges fixed from the historical red factor were reused. All branches share the same valid comparison support.

figure.name: figure07_boundary
figure.caption: The raw fixed edge jump is 5.586 encoded units; the new historical-BRDF replay jumps 3.372 billion. Boundary edges were fixed from the old factor before new-branch evaluation. This is a mechanism replay, not a valid new BRDF fit.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: At row 921, columns 980-981: new raw jump 5.586; new historical-BRDF replay jump 3.37e+09 encoded units.
Median absolute edge jump: new raw 15.383; historical replay 3.15e+09. The source cleanup does not remove a pathological model/reference prediction.

title: The main raw spectral-angle change is an encoding effect
intro: Old native encoding, old data recovered to the fixed encoding, and the new source were kept separate. Comparisons use the same pixel memberships, so coverage changes cannot create an apparent quality improvement.

figure.name: figure08_consistency
figure.caption: All 157 polygons use identical valid pixels. Recovering the old encoding accounts for most raw spectral-angle change; the remaining median pixel angle is about 0.00077 degrees. Variance and CV are descriptive numerical metrics, not physical validation.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: On 144,406 matched polygon pixels, median angle from old raw to new raw is 0.4743 degrees. After recovering the old encoding, it is only 0.000773 degrees. This residual does not establish physical accuracy.

Median within-polygon band CV is 0.232002 for new raw versus 0.231988 for the old fixed-encoding control: essentially unchanged, with a tiny increase. Median mean-band variance is 15,618 versus 15,617 encoded-unit squared. Do not call that improved homogeneity.

title: Keep the researcher labels and the sampling unit
intro: The canonical package index supplies membership. Experimental numeric spectra retain GlobalID, cover_category, species, flight identity, source hash, branch and pixel count. Approved physical extraction remains blocked.

figure.name: figure09_pft_spectra
figure.caption: Class medians and new-raw polygon IQR on matched support. The gray inverse-encoding control nearly overlays the new source; NIR differences versus old raw mainly reflect the removed band-specific offset. Non-vegetated & dead is absent, not reassigned.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: Matched sample: 157 non-overlapping polygon representatives and 144,406 memberships. Recorded classes are Evergreen 98, Woody shrub 29, Herbaceous 25 and Deciduous 5. Non-vegetated & dead is absent and is not invented or reassigned.

All-band scene comparison uses 6,678,404 common pixels. Raw-only comparison uses 6,683,944. Native mask changes affect 277 canonical polygon memberships before matching; common sampling removes this coverage confound.

title: Separation and identification answer different questions
intro: The package spectral_separability function ran 499 synchronized permutations with explicit equal weights on the ten discrete bands. It provides conditional pairwise tests, not physical purity or abundance. Polygon exchangeability is assumed; fine spatial confounding is untested, Holm adjustment is within branch, and across-branch comparisons are exploratory.

figure.name: figure10_separability
figure.caption: New-source polygon diagnostics: Evergreen/Herbaceous centroid shapes are only 1.07 degrees apart; Evergreen/Woody shrub has substantial IQR overlap. Distinct centroids or significant permutation tests do not establish reliable individual identification.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: Evergreen versus Herbaceous centroid angle is 1.07 degrees; Evergreen versus Woody shrub has mean band-IQR overlap 0.432. These are descriptions of the retained single-flight researcher categories.

Woody shrub remains difficult to identify. The new-raw held-polygon recalls are Deciduous 4/5, Evergreen 73/98, Herbaceous 17/25 and Woody shrub 13/29. Five deciduous identities are too few for a precise generalization claim.

title: No detected identification gain from the new raw source
intro: The actual evaluate_identifiability API used identical three-fold polygon-disjoint splits, training-only scaling, fixed C=1, and no pixel-level replication as training samples. All branches use the same 157 identities.

figure.name: figure11_identifiability
figure.caption: 157 non-overlapping polygon identities, three identical grouped folds, training-only standardization and fixed C=1. Old and new raw produce identical predictions and 66.8% balanced accuracy. Corrected bars are unsupported historical experiments; a higher score does not approve a correction.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: Old raw, old recovered encoding and new raw all score 66.829% balanced accuracy, with identical out-of-fold predictions. A conditional bootstrap of those fixed predictions has zero paired difference, but omits training/model uncertainty and does not establish population equivalence.

Historical topographic replay scores 71.7%, while historical BRDF replay scores 60.0%. These remain unsupported corrections. A higher classification score cannot establish correct physical reflectance or justify near-singular correction factors.

title: Spectral structure is largely retained; abundance stays unvalidated
intro: PCA summarizes the paired spectral distributions after bringing old data to the same numerical encoding. It is a descriptive figure, separate from the classifier training and test splits.

figure.name: figure12_pca
figure.caption: One descriptive pooled standardized PCA basis on paired polygon means; this visualization is not part of classifier training. Both representations retain nearly the same structure. No independent physical accuracy, species purity or abundance claim follows.
figure.analytical_status: Uncalibrated numerical observations; historical corrected branches are diagnostic only

findings: The nearly coincident paired structure is consistent with little change in interior polygon spectra after the encoding control. It does not establish transfer to another flight, site or year.

Abundance estimation is NOT_EVALUATED: no independently verified physical endmember library, fractional-cover ground truth or abundance-validation design was supplied. Category recognition is not an abundance-accuracy test.
